about: The STOP policy as data (owner decisions 2026-10-20 D4, D8 and the STOP rule changes; docs/archon/stop-policy.md). Read from origin/main by stop-check.sh, stop-scan.js and stop-approve.sh. A protected path: only the owner changes it. Approvals are given in chat in the list round and recorded by stop-approve.sh record (owner decision 2026-11-19).
migration_clause: a database migration once a production database exists (none yet)

categories.label: stop-contract-push
categories.text: pushing a contract change to the hub repo, or a spec edit that could break a consumer

categories.label: stop-db-migration
categories.text: a database migration once a production database exists (none yet)

categories.label: stop-auth-access
categories.text: authentication, authorization or the access matrix, SSO/SAML/WS-Security config, or how a user is identified

categories.label: stop-crypto-logging
categories.text: encryption, key handling, or what gets logged where personal data could be involved

categories.label: stop-delete-history
categories.text: deleting a branch, worktree, history or the audit trail whose content is not all in main, and any force-push

categories.label: stop-production-config
categories.text: production configuration once something runs in production (nothing does yet)

categories.label: stop-secret-value
categories.text: secrets: a secret value, a credential, a token or key that must not leak

categories.label: stop-deploy
categories.text: anything that changes what is deployed

categories.label: stop-governance
categories.text: the STOP rules, an agent's scope or allowlist, hooks, or the merge path (the #151 precedent)

standing_rules.until: the first production database (the P4 release tickets, TASK-31.x)
standing_rules.source: docs/memory.md, 2026-10-18 — No production database until the end stages; owner decision 2026-10-20 D4
owner decision 2026-10-20, STOP rule changes: production configuration is pre-approved until something runs in production; secrets stay STOP

standing_rules.until: never: deleting what is all in main loses nothing
standing_rules.source: owner decision 2026-10-20, STOP rule changes: deleting a branch or worktree through cleanup-merged.sh when all its content is in main is not a STOP item

judgement_rules: The contract agent's verdict binds: when it finds that a ticket needs no contract push, stop-contract-push may be removed with its verdict in the notes; a real push stays the owner's, per push (owner, 2026-10-18 23:22).

A change to an agent's scope or allowlist, a hook or the STOP rules is the owner's (the #151 precedent, owner 2026-10-19 09:43): these are the protected paths. Since 2026-11-19 the owner approves one in chat in the list round, per ticket and per named path (a governance entry with paths); a protected path no entry names still holds the merge.
The build-feature exception means a run does not pause on a STOP item; it never means the item is approved.

The supervisor (owner D15, 2026-10-20) is deployed local service: its units (.archon/systemd/**), its scripts and its decision schema are protected paths, and its switches /etc/delegator-supervisor/live and /etc/delegator-supervisor/recover are the owner's own acts (root-owned, created with sudo); no approval entry covers them.
